findings.title: Unvalidated argon2 nb_blocks causes heap out-of-bounds write/read
findings.evidence: argon2i_32() copies the attacker/caller-controlled nb_blocks straight into config.nb_blocks at c_monocypher.pyx:328 and sizes the scratch buffer with malloc(nb_blocks*1024) at c_monocypher.pyx:345, but never enforces Monocypher's documented contract 'nb_blocks: memory hardness, >= 8 * nb_lanes' (monocypher.h:160). In crypto_argon2 (monocypher.c:749-751) nb_lanes is 1, so segment_size = nb_blocks/4 and lane_size = segment_size*4. When nb_blocks is small this rounds lane_size down to 0, yet the 'fill first 2 blocks of each lane' loop still writes blocks[0] and blocks[1] (monocypher.c:772-778), i.e. 2048 bytes. For nb_blocks=1 (and 0), malloc only allocated 1024 (or 0) bytes, so blocks[1] is a 1024-byte heap out-of-bounds write reached directly through the public argon2i_32() call at c_monocypher.pyx:347. Additionally, for nb_blocks in {0,1,2,3} lane_size==0 makes last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 = blocks - 1 at monocypher.c:907, an out-of-bounds read of 1024 bytes before the buffer that is hashed into the returned key. No length/range check exists between the Python argument and the C call, so any caller supplying nb_blocks<8 triggers memory corruption.
